# Changed-line coverage (opt-in)

The default coverage gate is exact 100% line and branch coverage of the whole
application. A repository whose existing coverage is far below that can opt in to
a different gate instead of being blocked by it:

> Every line and branch the pull request **adds or modifies** must be covered,
> and the repository-wide line and branch coverage must not fall below the base
> revision's.

Nothing changes for a repository that does not opt in: with the setting unset
(or `exact`) the gate, its output and the assessment and approval wording are
the same as before.

## Enabling it

The mode lives only in the protected repository configuration
(`.github/clouseau.json`), which is a control path: changing it needs the
exact-revision owner confirmation like any other policy change.

```json
{ "version": 2, "...": "...", "coverage": { "mode": "changed_lines" } }
```

`coverage.mode` is `"exact"` (the default) or `"changed_lines"`; no other key is
accepted. The required verification step name stays
`Enforce 100% line and branch coverage`, because installed workflows already
require that name.

## Workflow wiring

`operation: coverage` switches mode only when **both** the protected `config`
says `changed_lines` **and** the workflow passes `coverage-base-ref`. Anything
else runs the exact gate, which is the stricter direction.

| Input | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `config` | The protected configuration. Pass the **base** revision's file (for example `git show "$BASE_SHA:.github/clouseau.json"`), never the contributor's. |
| `coverage-base-ref` | Base revision to diff against, for example the PR base SHA. The checkout needs its history (`fetch-depth: 0`). |
| `coverage-baseline` | JSON totals measured on the base revision: `{"lines":[total,covered],"branches":[total,covered]}`. |

# Quickstart: a new repository to its first auto-merged PR

This is the shortest verified path for a repository with no Clouseau files. It
links to the reference documents instead of repeating them. Every step below was
run in a fresh repository. Decide first which mode you want:

| Mode | You need | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Local receipt (`local_review.mode: optional` or `required`) | An authenticated `codex` or `claude` on your workstation | The PR carries a signed local review; CI only verifies it. No provider key |
| CI review (PRs without a receipt, `optional` mode) | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` secret (and `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` when `acceptance.grader` is `routed` or `typesafe`) | CI performs the AI review itself |

Without the CI secrets, a PR that has no valid receipt ends with the comment
`Clouseau review incomplete ... DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is not configured`; add the
secret and re-run the failed jobs.

## 1. Repository settings (before the first PR)

- Settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions: enable **Allow GitHub
  Actions to create and approve pull requests** (API:
  `gh api -X PUT repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/permissions/workflow -F can_approve_pull_request_reviews=true -f default_workflow_permissions=read`).
  The automatic approval depends on it (see the README's protected-merge
  requirements).
- Settings > General > Pull Requests: enable **Allow auto-merge** and squash
  merging. Private repositories on a plan without branch protection cannot enable
  it; see [the private-plan path](change-acceptance.md#controller-enforced-owner-merge-on-an-unavailable-private-plan)
  (`merge_mode` must then be `automatic` or `manual`, and the initial trust check

- Add `.github/CODEOWNERS` naming the owner when `merge_mode` is `automatic`.
- Runners: the reference workflow uses `ubuntu-latest`. Self-hosted pools must

- Pushing files under `.github/workflows/` needs a credential with the

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.

# Changed-line coverage (opt-in)

The default coverage gate is exact 100% line and branch coverage of the whole
application. A repository whose existing coverage is far below that can opt in to
a different gate instead of being blocked by it:

> Every line and branch the pull request **adds or modifies** must be covered,
> and the repository-wide line and branch coverage must not fall below the base
> revision's.

Nothing changes for a repository that does not opt in: with the setting unset
(or `exact`) the gate, its output and the assessment and approval wording are
the same as before.

## Enabling it

The mode lives only in the protected repository configuration
(`.github/clouseau.json`), which is a control path: changing it needs the
exact-revision owner confirmation like any other policy change.

```json
{ "version": 2, "...": "...", "coverage": { "mode": "changed_lines" } }
```

`coverage.mode` is `"exact"` (the default) or `"changed_lines"`; no other key is
accepted. The required verification step name stays
`Enforce 100% line and branch coverage`, because installed workflows already
require that name.

## Workflow wiring

`operation: coverage` switches mode only when **both** the protected `config`
says `changed_lines` **and** the workflow passes `coverage-base-ref`. Anything
else runs the exact gate, which is the stricter direction.

| Input | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `config` | The protected configuration. Pass the **base** revision's file (for example `git show "$BASE_SHA:.github/clouseau.json"`), never the contributor's. |
| `coverage-base-ref` | Base revision to diff against, for example the PR base SHA. The checkout needs its history (`fetch-depth: 0`). |
| `coverage-baseline` | JSON totals measured on the base revision: `{"lines":[total,covered],"branches":[total,covered]}`. |

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
